experiments.scope: H2 and H4 (proof.md Sections 4.3, 7 and 13.2-13.3). experiments/a0core.py rebuilds S, L*, the 222 classes from their descriptors and checks the published pair; trials 0..15 each choose (from SHAKE-256 of the seed) a class, a variant a0 of it and l among the 28 elements of L* whose row 16 can hold, and build a 37-step semi-free-start collision whose second-block state uses the variant (rows 16..21 by proposals with each row's fixed x-bits of E imposed, restarting from row 16 after 2^11 proposals at a row; row 22 by W22 proposals with its x-cells and two-bit conditions imposed, W7 drawn exactly from F7, W6 = W22 - s1(W20) - W15 - s0(W7) accepted iff in F6; rows 22..36 with the variant's W8; W0..W5 by the inverse expansion; CV1 by inverting steps 7..0). A trial returns CV1||M1 and CV1||M1' (96 bytes each) iff: the Step-2 equations of (CV1, a0) give exactly W0..W13 of both members, the two 37-step outputs are equal, M1 != M1', every cell of rows -4..36 (W6/W7 XOR cells excepted) and every printed two-bit condition of rows 8..36 holds, a0 is in G and in its class, and W8 differs from the published one. Trials 16..255 return no pair by design.
experiments.hypothesis: Returned pairs: about 16 (trials 0..15; a trial can fail only by exhausting its proposal budget). Full collisions of the complete target: 0 (these are semi-free-start collisions from CV1, not from the IV; anyone can verify them offline with the 37-step compression). This tests that A0-variants of S (proof.md Lemma 4.2, 4.3) are valid dense parts that reach full 37-step semi-free-start collisions through every cell of rows 16..36 with their own W8 (Lemma 7.1). It does not estimate q3. Observations (participant numbers): class_index, variant_index, l, checks_passed, restarts, proposals_row16, proposals_tail. A local emulation of the public-seed request (organizer seed protocol, no holdout nonce) returned 16 pairs, all verified with the repository verifier (classes and variants drawn from the 222 classes).

experiments.scope: H1, H3, H5 (proof.md Sections 5, 8, 9 and 13.3). The same program; trials 0..7 each run the counted online program (proof.md Section 8) on seed-drawn first blocks (two uniform words from SHAKE-256 of the seed per first block; real 37-step compressions) until a first block has a passing class (at most 64 first blocks), processing at most two passing classes of it: the bit-sliced W7 program of all 222 classes, the bit-sliced W6 programs of every batch (four batches per program), the lane scan, the good pairs in groups of four 64-bit lanes (u = W0 + s0(W1)), the presence-word and bit test of row 16 for every good pair, rows 17..36 for every row-16 pass. Every lane of every batch is checked against the scalar W6 definition, the u of every good pair against the scalar W0 + s0(W1), every good pair against the Step-2 equations (W7x = c7 - A_{-1} in F7, W6x in F6), and up to 12 good pairs against every cell of rows -4..15 for all 32 elements of L*. A trial returns the complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (l = 13) of its first good pair iff all checks passed. Trials 8..255 return no pair by design.
experiments.hypothesis: Full collisions: 0 (rows 16..36 are not expected to hold). Mismatches of every kind: 0. Returned pairs: those trials whose first passing first block had a W6 pass in its first two passing classes (about half; good pairs are bursty). Observations (participant numbers): first_blocks, w7_classes, classes_processed, good_pairs, row16_pairs, counted_ops, lane_mismatches, filter_mismatches, cell_mismatches, pairs_cell_checked. A local emulation of the public-seed request returned 2 pairs with 0 mismatches (2768 good pairs in all). This tests the correctness of the counted bit-sliced filters and of the four-lane group (H5), the per-variant Step-2 equations and the validity of good pairs through row 15 (Lemma 4.3) on organizer-seeded first blocks (H1); it does not test q3.
